Definition: properly, an envelope, i.e. darkness (or density, 2 Chronicles 4:17); specifically, a (scud) cloud; also a copse
BiblicalUsage: This is the word for a cloud — usually a thick, heavy one. God comes to Moses 'in a thick cloud' on Sinai; Elijah's servant spots 'a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand' before the rain breaks; Job's friends say thick clouds hide God from seeing; and David pictures God's pavilion wrapped in dark waters and thick clouds.
TheologicalSignificance: Clouds in Scripture are God's covering — He hides in them and reveals Himself through them at the same time. I believe that is honest about how God works: He is near and real, and still beyond my full sight, and the cloud reminds me to trust what He has said even when I cannot see Him clearly.
